Both always-on checks (xml parse, manifest consistency) and all three declared checkers (record-triggered-flow-patterns, flow-element-naming-conventions, flow-governance) exit 0 with the same output as the pre-rebuild test run, check-outputs reports ok with nothing missing/empty/malformed, and the one declared manual test remains a well-formed Given/When/Then naming observable outcomes, deferred to the milestone gate. confidence_rationale: Every declared acceptance test either ran to an observed exit code or was correctly classified as manual; both always-on checks completed; check-outputs was ok; no checker was missing and no command test needed the deny-list.

process_observations.observation: The F-38 fix is narrowly scoped: only the FlowTest and deploy-order.md changed between the pre- and post-rebuild artefacts, confirmed by direct grep of the FlowTest's testPoints block (InputTriggeringRecordInitial now present at line 10) and by the builder's own SHA-256 comparison of the other five declared outputs. All three declared checkers reproduced byte-identical stdout to the pre-rebuild test run, which is exactly what an unchanged flow XML should produce.

The manifest is a clean two-way match: three metadata members (Flow, FlowTest, Settings:Flow) each have exactly one file and each file derives exactly one member, with no wildcard members and no orphaned files. Unchanged from the pre-rebuild run since package.xml was not touched by the F-38 fix.

check_flow_element_naming_conventions.py still reports four W-FAULT-TARGET warnings because every fault path on this before-save flow reconverges on a Decision element instead of a LogFault_<Parent> target; deploy-order.md already records this as a library gap rather than a defect in this artefact. Advisory only, exit 0, unchanged by the rebuild.

deploy-order.md still carries the derived CasePriority value mapping (Severity 1 -> High, Premier -> High, else Medium) as UNVERIFIED rather than answered by a clarification; unrelated to the F-38 fix and still unresolved by this run, since step-tester does not adjudicate Salesforce design questions. Carried forward to the milestone gate unchanged.
M4-S03 is tested again with zero failures after the F-38 rebuild, and one manual test remains deferred to the milestone gate.
